summary: The Alaska Court System's weekly dispositions report, re-run early Monday, records 42 Interior criminal cases closed between Nov. 16 and Nov. 20: a third-degree assault charge dismissed by prosecutors a day after it was filed, a second-degree robbery count dismissed, convictions entered at Fairbanks for felony assault, DUI and reckless driving, and three Fairbanks case numbers closed without any charge ever being filed. Alaska State Troopers report two DUI arrests in the Fairbanks area over the weekend and a vehicle collision on Farmer's Loop Road, and Fairbanks Police report four arrests on Sunday. The court's weekly charges report for Nov. 16-22 lists 39 criminal cases filed at Fairbanks and none at Nenana, Healy or Delta Junction.

entries.title: Felony assault charge dismissed: Jerald Curtis Waters
body: A charge of assault in the third degree against Jerald Curtis Waters was dismissed by prosecutors on Nov. 17, the day after the case was opened at Fairbanks. The single count alleged placing another person in fear of imminent injury with a weapon. The offense date was Nov. 16 at Fairbanks.
Case 4FA-26-02301CR. The court record states the dismissal was by the prosecution and gives no further reason.

entries.title: Robbery charge dismissed: Michael Aaron Tritt
body: Two charges against Michael Aaron Tritt were dismissed by prosecutors on Nov. 19: robbery in the second degree, taking property by using force to prevent resistance, and assault in the fourth degree, recklessly injuring another person. The offense date was Nov. 14 at Fairbanks.

entries.title: Five cases closed, two convictions: Ishi Santana Sarten
body: Five Fairbanks criminal cases against Ishi Santana Sarten were closed on Nov. 20. Two ended in convictions after guilty pleas: one count of criminal trespass in the second degree, entering or remaining unlawfully on premises, and one count of indecent exposure in the second degree, which the court records as a Class B misdemeanor.
Three further counts of criminal trespass in the second degree were dismissed under a plea agreement in another case. The five offense dates run from Oct. 3 to Oct. 17 at Fairbanks.

body: Two Fairbanks cases against Brandon Moore were closed on Nov. 19. All three counts of violating a domestic violence protective order were dismissed in the furtherance of justice. The offense dates were April 25 and May 31 at Fairbanks.

entries.title: Three Fairbanks cases closed with no charges filed
body: Three criminal case numbers opened at the Fairbanks court in mid-November were closed without any charging document being filed, so no charge was ever brought in any of them. Each file carries a single entry recording a charging document pending or not filed.

4FA-26-02307CR, State of Alaska vs. Shay Pitka, offense date Nov. 18, closed Nov. 18. 4FA-26-02316CR, State of Alaska vs. Katrina Albert, offense date Nov. 19, closed Nov. 20. 4FA-26-02317CR, State of Alaska vs. Arlo Charles Leroy Smoke, offense date Nov. 19, closed Nov. 20.
None of the three is charged with an offense on the face of the court record, and none is convicted of one.

entries.title: DUI arrest: Shannon Rice
body: Shannon Rice was arrested on a charge of driving under the influence, operating a vehicle while impaired by alcohol. Near Cushman Street, Fairbanks, Nov. 21; Alaska State Troopers. Case 4FA-26-02324CR; arraignment Nov. 27.

Troopers say they stopped a Ford F-250 after seeing a non-functioning license plate light, that Rice admitted to recently consuming alcohol and showed signs of impairment, and that a breath test at the Fairbanks trooper post recorded a breath alcohol concentration of 0.085. Rice was taken to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.
The court file opened behind the arrest records no charge as yet, so no charge class is given here.

body: Alaska State Troopers say that at about 11:20 p.m. on Nov. 1 they responded to a report of a possible head-on collision on Farmer's Loop Road in Fairbanks, and that the collision was a sideswipe with no injuries reported. No arrest or charge is stated.
Incident AK26018151. The report was posted to the trooper dispatch on Nov. 23.
